findings.title: ChunkedReader discards any 2 bytes as the chunk footer instead of validating CRLF (request smuggling)
findings.evidence:
ChunkedReader never checks the chunk terminator. After reading chunk-data it sets self._bytes_to_discard = 2 (an integer count, line 197), and the discard branch at lines 163-171 extracts up to that many bytes and merely decrements the counter (self._bytes_to_discard -= len(data), line 167); the extracted bytes are compared against nothing, unlike upstream h11 0.16.0 which stores the literal b'
' and raises LocalProtocolError('malformed chunk footer') on mismatch (fix for CVE-2025-43859 / GHSA-vqfr-h8mv-ghfj, CVSS 9.1). Reachability: a remote peer simply frames its body with Transfer-Encoding: chunked, which selects this reader via READERS[SEND_BODY]['chunked'] (h11/_readers.py:243). Confirmed by executing the audited code: feeding b'5
helloXY0

' or b'5
hello

0

' to ChunkedReader yields Data(b'hello') followed by EndOfMessage instead of a RemoteProtocolError, i.e. 'XY' and even a bare LF are silently accepted as the required CRLF chunk delimiter. RFC 7230 requires CRLF after chunk-data, so any intermediary that parses the delimiter strictly (or differently) frames the same byte stream differently, producing exactly the front-end/back-end parsing discrepancy (smuggling/body desync) that the upstream security fix addresses.

findings.title: Unbounded Content-Length digit length reaches int() and raises uncaught ValueError (remote DoS)
findings.evidence:
_body_framing returns ('content-length', (int(content_lengths[0]),)) at h11/_connection.py:123, converting the raw attacker-controlled header value to a Python int. The guard added upstream in 0.15.0 (CONTENT_LENGTH_MAX_DIGITS = 20, checked in h11/_headers.py before the value is stored; the audited copy only validates it against /[0-9]+/ at h11/_headers.py:175) is absent, so a peer can send up to max_incomplete_event_size (16 KiB default) of digits. Confirmed by execution: h11.Connection(h11.SERVER).receive_data(b'GET / HTTP/1.1
Host: x
Content-Length: ' + b'9'*5000 + b'

') followed by next_event() raises ValueError('Exceeds the limit (4300 digits) for integer string conversion') on CPython >= 3.11 rather than h11.RemoteProtocolError. This violates next_event()'s documented contract that no exception other than ProtocolError is emitted, so callers that only catch h11.ProtocolError (the expected error-handling pattern, e.g. HTTP servers) get an unhandled exception that aborts the request/connection; on interpreters without the int-conversion limit the same input forces parsing of a multi-kilobyte integer, which is the DoS the upstream cap was introduced to prevent.
